statements.t: We believe this is a balanced initial outlook given potential risks to the pace of data center build-outs and potential upside if strength in modular activation activity continues or the demand profile broadens.
We are excited about these fundamental improvements to our business trajectory and intend to execute against these opportunities on behalf of our shareholders."

Matt Jacobsen, Chief Financial Officer of WillScot, commented, "Third quarter 2026 revenues of $601 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $234 million exceeded our outlook due to continued strong leasing and services revenue growth.

Jacobsen continued, "Incorporating year-to-date 2026 results and ongoing activation levels, we are raising our 2026 outlook for revenue to $2.340 billion and maintaining Adjusted EBITDA at $920 million.
Relative to our prior guidance, our expectations for modular activations and delivery and installation revenues in the fourth quarter have increased meaningfully.
With these increases and the continued growth in our order book, we expect unit work order production levels to remain elevated.
As we balance absolute debt reduction with investments in attractive opportunities to drive Adjusted EBITDA growth, we expect leverage to be approaching 3.0x as we exit 2027."
The Company updated its full year 2026 outlook provided in August 2026.
Although we provide outlooks for Adjusted EBITDA and Net CAPEX that we believe will be achieved, we cannot accurately predict all the components of the Adjusted EBITDA and Net CAPEX calculations.

The Company provides Adjusted EBITDA and Net CAPEX guidance because we believe that Adjusted EBITDA and Net CAPEX, when viewed with our results under GAAP, provides useful information for the reasons noted below.

statements.t: We also provide other services to our customers, including technical expertise and oversight regarding building design and permitting, site preparation, and project management, including expansion or contraction of installed space based on changes in project requirements.

These indicators, among others, support our demand forecast for our two largest end markets, the commercial and industrial sector and the construction and infrastructure market, which collectively accounted for approximately 87% of our revenues for the nine months ended September 30, 2026.

We believe these actions will reduce expected annual real estate cost increases, leave adequate idle fleet to meet future projected demand, and maintain market coverage and customer service capabilities.

As of September 30, 2026, we expect the initiative to result in total future costs of approximately $41 million, consisting of rental equipment disposal costs of approximately $26 million and rental equipment relocation costs of approximately $15 million.

We intend to continue our quarterly dividend program, subject to Board of Directors and Dividend Committee approval, the requirements of our debt instruments, and based on available cash flow, capital allocation priorities, and market conditions.
